metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.161

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.161
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.161
- Datum: 08.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear H. & M. now we have to economise VIA AIR MAIL paper
as the airmail takes from Rio only 5 grammes. We had
an extremely quiet voyage and are both
again restored after the heavy strain of Newyork
- I have never been so down as S. S. Uruguay
in these last weeks and Lotte too has not been too
well. What we want both is some months in
a quiet place and not hotellife; we hope to find
this near Rio. In America you feel already
the war in the atmosphere, the preparations
are tremendous and life became still more ex-
peansive than it was - I believe we have seen
for the last time the splendour and the luxu
ry there as this war will unfortunately be
a very long one and the expenses are simply
fantastic. We have here with the sister of
Morgentau, who has the whole financial prepa
ration in hand, her husband is from here
and arched since many years in Newyork;
I start already learning better Portuguese
as I shall stay at least six months here -
we do not know when it will possible to
go to the States and if it will be the right
thing for us who are longing to have rest
from travelling; it was hard for us to leave
Eva behind but we feel that she is better
here with her "auntie" Han with us
who do not know where to we go; perhaps
I have to lecture again in Argentine. I be-
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Stempel 'Moore-McCormack Lines' oben links.

pages.transcription:
lieve I was right to go to Brazil where I have
a right for permanent stay while in Ame
rica I was only a visitor and in case of
war I would have had all these little
annoyances as a foreigner (a friendly one
in this case). I hope you have got my letter
about the house; it is important for me
that you dispose in such a way that you
can ~~dispose~~ take it over completely - dont
think about me, I have written all in the
chimney what I had (as one said in short)
and I feel happy with everything you
can use of what I have - my clothes
shoes, furniture and so on. I hear that
clothing, suits etc are difficult to get (in England!)
and so you could let change some of
mine for Manfred [?] and some of
other things for you. We want here
nothing of all that and I feel, I shall
never use it any more. Please make
me the pleasure to use everything and
everything as if it were yours. As soon
as we have a definitive adress we shall
write immediately to you. Kindest regards
to you all. Yours Stefan Zweig
We write this still on the ____________
ship and you shall soon have news from us. My
book will be sent directly to you by the publisher
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Fortsetzung. Am linken Rand vertikal geschrieben: 'and I hope to come through soon with the other, when I wrote in Ossining.'

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift Zweigs. Einige wenige Wörter wie 'Manfred' sind aufgrund der Tintenführung leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext der Korrespondenz eindeutig.
